searches.reason: Explore learning recurrent states that distinguish persistent preferences from immediate next-item demand through auxiliary future-horizon supervision. Unlike adding another retention gate or recent-history residual, this changes what the GRU representation learns. Require causal inputs, auxiliary labels drawn only from training histories, and a single next-item scoring head at inference.

searches.reason: Challenge the assumption that interaction order alone identifies current intent. Available timestamp gaps could help a GRU distinguish continuous activity from returns after long absences. Seek practical time-conditioned recurrent dynamics beyond scalar state decay, with a time-blind control and explicit timestamp availability at inference; do not infer compatibility, ownership needs or mood from time gaps.
